comments.author: participant1
comments.body:
I made a vim autocmd to remove then when I enter Neovim and add them back when I exit.
Currently using `AstroNvim` but this can be converted easily to a normal nvim autocmds:

NOTE: You will need to put the `window_padding ` on one line !

Note that I am currently using the `sd` command which is a cross-platform remplacement for the `sed` command available on unix systems as I'm am currently using Windows Powershell.

On `VimEnter`
```
{
    event = "VimEnter",
    desc = "Remove WezTerm padding when entering Neovim",
    group = "removeshellspaddings",
    command = ":<nick> !sd -F '{ left = 20, right = 20, top = 15, bottom = 15 }' '{ left = 0, right = 0, top = 0, bottom = 0 }' '<add your wezterm config file path here>'"
},
```

On `VimLeavePre`
```
{
    event = "VimLeavePre",
    desc = "Add WezTerm padding padding back when exiting Neovim",
    group = "addshellspaddings",
    command = ":<nick> !sd -F '{ left = 0, right = 0, top = 0, bottom = 0 }' '{ left = 20, right = 20, top = 15, bottom = 15 }' '<add your wezterm config file path here>'"
},
```

It could be way easier if wezterm could have a command with the wezterm CLI.

participant6
comments.body:
There’s an approach without specifying the path to the wezterm configuration.
It also works if for some reason nvim doesn't see the path or there is no way to use [this](https://github.com/participant2/wezterm/discussions/4117) solution (the tab title doesn't change in wsl when you open nvim).
However, the bottom padding will still remain for me.

wezterm configuration
```lua
local padding = {
  left = '1cell',
  right = '1cell',
  top = '0.5cell',
  bottom = '0.5cell',
}

wezterm.on('user-var-changed', function(window, pane, name, value)
  if name == "NVIM_ENTER" then
    local overrides = window:get_config_overrides() or {}
    if value == "1" then
      overrides.window_padding = {
        left = 0,
        right = 0,
        top = 0,
        bottom = 0
      }
    else
      overrides.window_padding = padding
    end
    window:set_config_overrides(overrides)
  end
end)
```

neovim configuration
```lua
local autocmd = vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd

autocmd("VimEnter", {
  callback = function()
    --NVIM_ENTER=1
    vim.cmd([[call chansend(v:stderr, "\033]1337;SetUserVar=NVIM_ENTER=MQ==\007")]])
  end,
})

autocmd("VimLeavePre", {
  callback = function()
    --NVIM_ENTER=0
    vim.cmd([[call chansend(v:stderr, "\033]1337;SetUserVar=NVIM_ENTER=MA==\007")]])
  end,
})
```

comments.author: participant9
comments.body:
If you've ever used other terminals, you can notice that they also have "paddings", but on kitty for example the content is centered, that is why it's not looking that bad, but in wezterm the default content alignment is top-left. But you can change that in _**nightly**_ builds of wezterm, [here is documentation](https://wezterm.org/config/lua/config/window_content_alignment.html) or code snippet to center content:
```lua
config.window_content_alignment = {
  horizontal = 'Center',
  vertical = 'Center',
}
```
with that and padding 0, it will looks much better (at least for me), and looks at least as good as in kitty.

comments.author: participant10
comments.body:
there been any progress on this? participant6's solution works but seems a little jank to go about checking every `user-var-changed` event.

participant1's solution is suboptimal because (1) it makes every wezterm window's padding the same so having one window with neovim and another with plain text makes one or the other have the weird padding and (2) it requires write permissions to the config file which doesn't work for me: I have Nix creating config files as symlinks to read-only files.
> With normal autocmds on neovim and using `sed`, it would probably look like this:
> 
> ```
> -- Commands when Vim start
> vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("VimEnter", {
>   command = ":<nick> !sed -i -e 's/{ left = 20, right = 20, top = 15, bottom = 15 }/{ left = 0, right = 0, top = 0, bottom = 0 }/g' '<add your wezterm config file path here>'",
> })
> 
> -- Commands when just before Vim exits
> vim.api.nvim_create_autocmd("VimLeavePre", {
>   command = ":<nick> !sed -i -e 's/{ left = 0, right = 0, top = 0, bottom = 0 }/{ left = 20, right = 20, top = 15, bottom = 15 }/g' '<add your wezterm config file path here>'",
> })
> ```

Also, to people coming here with LazyVim, a la [this dicussion](https://github.com/LazyVim/LazyVim/issues/2592#issuecomment-2015093693), the `VimEnter` event doesn't quite work the way you might want. Just stick the `VimEnter` autocmd in `options.lua`.

comments.author: participant2
comments.body:
I don't think there is anything to fix here in wezterm; it sounds like the issue is with the selected nvim theme not working well with transparency.  I think that the user-var solution is a reasonable sounding workaround for that, but I think a better fix is to fix the nvim theme to work better with transparency, or not use transparency.

A simple vim theme like my own https://gist.github.com/participant2/afea18dba82825663712c882947e4aa4 leaves the color selection largely to the terminal and doesn't have this sort of problem.
